questions.original_prompt: State two advantages of using CNG over petrol or diesel. [BL-2]
questions.source_answer_unverified: ➢ Lower emissions: CNG produces less CO₂, CO, NOx, and particulate matter than petrol or diesel. ➢ Cost-effective and safer: CNG is generally cheaper per energy unit and less flammable than petrol.

questions.original_prompt: Why is Hythane considered a cleaner fuel? [BL-3]
questions.source_answer_unverified: ➢ Hythane is a mixture of methane (≈80%) and hydrogen (≈20%). ➢ Hydrogen addition reduces CO₂ and particulate emissions during combustion. ➢ It also improves engine efficiency and produces cleaner exhaust gases compared to CNG or petrol.
questions.selection_reason: Source-authored Q&A; broad emissions, safety and ranking claims need qualification before reuse.

questions.original_prompt: Which is much preferred among the three-LPG,CNG, & Hythane? [BL-3]
questions.source_answer_unverified: Hythane is considered the most environmentally friendly & efficient among LPG, CNG because it contains H2(18-20%), which promotes more complete combustion of methane. It produces significantly lower emissions of carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, nitrogen oxides & carbon dioxide. Hythane offers higher fuel efficiency & better performance than CNG alone. It serves as a transition fuel towards a hydrogen-based future, using existing CNG infrastructure with minor modifications.
questions.selection_reason: Source-authored Q&A; broad emissions, safety and ranking claims need qualification before reuse.

questions.original_prompt: Explain the use of UV–Visible spectroscopy for pollutant analysis in dye industries.
source_answer_unverified: UV–Visible spectroscopy is widely used to monitor organic dye pollutants. Dye molecules contain chromophores that absorb visible light, producing characteristic absorption peaks. The concentration of dye effluents is determined using the Beer–Lambert law:
Detection of residual dyes in wastewater.
Identifying different dye structures by their λmax.
Evaluating color removal efficiency in treatment plants.
The method is fast, non-destructive, and suitable for continuous effluent monitoring.

questions.original_prompt: Explain the significance of IR spectroscopy in night vision systems and PUC CO sensors.
source_answer_unverified: Objects emit IR radiation depending on temperature. IR detectors capture this thermal radiation (7–14 μm for thermal IR) and convert it into an electronic signal. The image generated provides visibility in complete darkness. Used in security, surveillance, and rescue.

CO molecules absorb IR radiation at ~4.6 μm. When IR radiation passes through vehicle exhaust, CO absorbs specific wavelengths, causing reduced transmission. The detector measures this drop to calculate CO concentration. Used in Pollution Under Control (PUC) systems.

questions.original_prompt: Describe Raman spectroscopy and its application in tumour detection.
source_answer_unverified: Raman spectroscopy is based on the Raman effect (inelastic scattering). When monochromatic light (laser) interacts with molecules, most photons scatter elastically, while a small fraction scatter with shifted energy. These energy shifts correspond to molecular vibrations.
Cancer tissues show altered biochemical composition.
Allows real-time, non-invasive detection of cancerous regions.
Used in breast, brain, and oral cancer diagnosis.
